title: Rami bar Abba (I)
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: Hyman gives his true name as Rabbi Ami bar Abba, and in short Rami bar Ami.

He was Rav Huna’s student, as in [Eruvin 10a](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.10a.7): “Rav Yosef said: I have not heard this teaching. Abaye said to him … On this you told us, for Rami bar Abba said it in Rav Huna’s name” (Hyman proposes this reading there at [5a](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.5a.13), where he considers Rami bar Chama erroneous; and so the [Rosh](https://www.sefaria.org/Rosh_on_Eruvin.1.5) and, according to Hyman, Dikdukei Soferim cite Rami bar Abba). There, [61a](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.61a.9): Rav Yosef reports a teaching that Rami bar Abba gave in Rav Huna’s name.[^7]

In [Eruvin 100b](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.100b.7): Rami bar Abba speaks in Rav Assi’s name. In [Berakhot 59b](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.59b.2-3) and [Shabbat 151b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.151b.10): Hyman cites Rami bar Avi speaking in Rabbi Yitzchak’s name.

In [Shabbat 20b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.20b.3) he disagrees with Rav Yosef. For the most part his precious words that remain to us are in aggadah, as in [Nedarim 32a](https://www.sefaria.org/Nedarim.32a.17-32b.4): “Rabbi Ami bar Abba said: Eliezer was equal to all of them”; “Rabbi Ami bar Abba said: Abraham recognized his Creator at three years old, as it is said ‘Ekev’ — its numerical value is 172”; “Rami bar Abba said: The Satan — its numerical value is 364”; “Rami bar Abba said: It is written Avram and it is written Avraham — at first He made him king,” etc.; and “Rami bar Abba said: What is the meaning of what is written, ‘a small city,’” etc.
Hyman concludes from this that Rami and Rabbi Ami are one.

He likewise expounded numerical values, as in [Megillah 15b](https://www.sefaria.org/Megillah.15b.19), where he said: “The sons of Haman were two hundred and eight, as it is said ‘and the multitude of his sons’ (verov), whose numerical value is 208.”

He is likewise mentioned in [Beitzah 25a](https://www.sefaria.org/Beitzah.25a.12): “Rami bar Abba said: The flaying and cutting up of the burnt-offering — from here the Torah teaches proper conduct,” etc. [Beitzah 25b](https://www.sefaria.org/Beitzah.25b.3-4), he said: “The sea squill cuts off the feet of the wicked; young trees cut off the feet of butchers and of those who have relations with menstruants,” etc.
In [Sanhedrin 19a](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.19a.12) he relates of the enactments that Rabbi Yose enacted in Tzippori.
In [Kiddushin 72a](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.72a.3) he said: “The pride (glory) of Babylonia is Shunya, and Guvya is the pride of the Seashore district.”

In [Eruvin 64b](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.64b.4) he said: “A mil’s walk and a little sleep dispel wine.” On this Rav Nachman speaks in Rabbah bar Avuha’s name: “They taught this only of one who drank,” etc.; Hyman attributes this juxtaposition to the Gemara’s arrangement and says it does not refer to Rami bar Ami’s words.

In halakhah he is mentioned in [Niddah 20a](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.20a.14-15): “Rabbi Ami bar Abba said: And all of them, deeper than this — impure; lighter than this — pure”; and some say, “Rami bar Abba said: And all of them, deeper than this — pure; lighter than this — pure.” Hyman concludes from this that Rabbi Ami bar Abba and Rami bar Abba are one. There is also …

notes.text: Missing ויש[1] ending and footnote keep p011 held. Preserve Rami barAmi in p001/p010 and the source’s barAvi in p003 rather than silently harmonizing all to Abba. Saved Davidson Beitzah25b identifies חצובא as SEA SQUILL, not caper, and נטיעה as young trees. Numerals3/172/364/208 and both deeper/lighter rulings remain as supplied. Hyman’s identity inference is attributed.

The numerical claim 208 is preserved as Hyman gives it. The supplied quotation writes ורוב, while the consonantal form ורב has value 208 (6 + 200 + 2); including the additional ו in ורוב would give 214. This explains the spelling distinction without silently changing Hyman’s quoted letters or numerical claim. The two deeper/lighter rulings, ages and other numerical values remain unchanged.

Hyman’s printed entry (vol. III, p. 1100) ends with ויש, “There is also,” immediately before the separate heading for Rami bar Abba (II). The Wikisource footnote says, “The sentence continues in the next entry.” That entry begins with the synagogue-building case in Megillah 26b. The two entries retain their separate headings.

Hyman’s two versions are translated as printed. In the consulted Niddah 20a, Rabbi Ami bar Abba’s version makes both darker and lighter shades impure, with an exception for black. The version attributed to Rami bar Abba makes both shades pure, also with an exception for black. Bar Kappara gives a separate ruling that makes darker shades impure and lighter shades pure, with an exception for the color of diluted wine.

The consulted Eruvin 5a gives Rami bar Chama, while the Vilna edition of the Rosh (Eruvin 1:5) gives Rami bar Abba. The consulted Eruvin 10a and 61a:9 also give bar Abba in the transmission from Rav Huna. Hyman’s print and the consulted Berakhot 59b give bar Abba where the supplied transcription gives bar Avi. The consulted Shabbat 151b names Rami bar Abba in a different statement. In Eruvin 64b, the name in the saying about wine is bar Abba. Hyman writes bar Ami in his comment on how that passage was arranged.

The cited sayings about Abraham and the small city span Nedarim 32a–b. The statement about flaying the burnt offering crosses from Beitzah 25a to 25b. The consulted Kiddushin 72a places both Shunya and Guvya in the line praising Haveil Yamma, which the passage calls the glory of Babylonia. Hyman’s wording gives Shunya and Guvya different descriptions.

[Seder HaDorot 3243](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=3243&lang=en) also discusses bar Ami and bar Abba in the Eruvin tradition. [Eruvin 5a:13](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.5a.13) reads bar Chama, while the [Rosh](https://www.sefaria.org/Rosh_on_Eruvin.1.5) reads bar Abba. In [Berakhot 59b:2–3](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.59b.2-3), bar Abba cites Rav Yitzchak. [Shabbat 151b:10](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.151b.10) has bar Abba speaking without naming a source at that point. Hyman’s printed sigla and his proposed relationships between the names remain distinct.
